title: Convert cold-start/autoscale postmortem actions into serving PRD requirements and acceptance tests
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Summary: After a traffic surge on 2026-01-28 the autoscaling path introduced extended cold-start latencies (p95 > 2s and p99 > 10s for text-generation routes) while new GPU nodes initialized and KV caches warmed. The postmortem identified three classes of contributing factors: (1) no pre-warm policy for predicted surge windows, (2) aggressive scale-to-zero behavior combined with slow model initialization on certain hardware, and (3) insufficient synthetic canary traffic and gap in observability for early warning. This ticket translates the postmortem action items into concrete PRD requirement updates and acceptance criteria for the model-serving product to prevent regressions and make rollouts testable.
motivation_and_goals: Ensure future deployments and autoscaling behaviors meet latency SLOs during traffic spikes by adding deterministic guardrails: pre-warm thresholds, safe rollback criteria, SLO-driven routing, and synthetic canary tests integrated into the release pipeline. Reduce customer-facing latency spikes and avoid SLA breaches during scale events.
requirements: R1: Pre-warm Policy - Support declarative pre-warm configurations per deployment with parameters: min_instances, prewarm_lead_time, and warmup_probe_path. Default behavior: maintain min_instances >= 1 for the first 10 minutes after a detected surge pattern.

R2: Graceful Scale-to-Zero Controls - Add cooldown window and hysteresis controls to inhibit scale-to-zero within a configurable window after a sustained increase in requests (>30% over baseline for 5 minutes).

R3: Fast-Path Model Variant - Allow pinning a lightweight model variant (lower memory/quantized) for warm-up traffic that accepts the same API but returns immediately cached or low-cost responses while full model is initializing.

R4: SLO-Based Routing & Traffic Shaping - Introduce a controller that monitors p50/p95/p99 latencies and if p95 exceeds threshold for 3 consecutive evaluation windows, automatically route new requests to a fallback model variant or previously warmed capacity.

R5: Synthetic Canary Automation - Integrate synthetic spike tests into the canary rollout pipeline: a configurable spike profile that generates concurrent requests with a target QPS and verifies tail latency and error budgets before advancing rollout.

R6: Observability Enhancements - Emit new high-cardinality markers for 'initialization_phase' and 'prewarm_source' in traces; surface a dedicated dashboard for cold-start metrics (init_time, kv_cache_warm_time, first_token_latency).

R7: Runbook & Rollback Criteria - Codify clear rollback criteria tied to observable thresholds (e.g., if p95 > 1.5s and error_rate > 0.5% for 2 minutes), include automated rollback trigger as opt-in per deployment.
R8: Acceptance Tests & CI Integration - Add automated CI scenarios (chaos/spike/blackout) that must pass before runtime-1.20 can be released to production clusters.
R9: API/Console UX - Console should expose pre-warm controls, predicted cost estimate for pre-warm, and a visualization of warm-up progress (instances warmed, cache hit ratio).
acceptance_criteria: AC1: When pre-warm is enabled with min_instances=2 and prewarm_lead_time=5m, simulated spike (2x baseline QPS for 3 minutes) must keep route p95 latency < 800ms 95% of the time and p99 < 2s during the surge.

AC2: With scale-to-zero cooldown set to 10m, a sustained increase >30% for 5 minutes must not scale to zero and new instances must be provisioned within SLA-defined time windows (new_instance_ready < 90s median).
AC3: Synthetic canary spike must run as part of canary promotion and must not advance rollout if any canary run records p95 > 1s or error_rate > 0.2%.

AC4: Observability - Traces for initialization_phase and metric kv_cache_warm_time must be available for every deployment within 24 hours of release; dashboard shows warm-up percent and last warm-up duration for each model-version/region.

AC5: Fast-path fallback - If the controller routes traffic to the fast-path variant, end-to-end correctness tests (response schema and sampling quality checks) must pass with no more than 5% degradation in automated quality signals compared to baseline.
AC6: CI - The release gate requires passing chaos spike test (simulate node provisioning delay of 30s) with no more than 2% customer-facing errors and with alerting firing for any p99 violation.
AC7: Runbook verification - Running the documented rollback playbook on a staging incident must reliably recover SLO-compliant latencies within 5 minutes when triggered.

AC8: Cost visibility - Console must display an estimate of incremental cost for pre-warm per hour and an expected cost impact for a 10-minute surge; values should compute within acceptable error bounds (<10% error compared to actual in a test cluster).
AC9: End-to-end automation - Enabling pre-warm and synthetic canary for a new deployment should be doable through the API and console in under 2 minutes with predictable defaults.
design_and_tradeoffs: Tradeoffs considered: pre-warm increases short-term spend; we mitigate via predictive heuristics (traffic pattern detection) and conservative defaults. Fast-path model variants trade quality for speed—we require inline quality checks and explicit opt-in per customer. Synthetic canaries add time to rollouts but provide critical protection; we will parallelize canary traffic where possible to reduce wall-clock time.
decisions: D1: Default pre-warm off; opt-in per deployment. Customers with high SLOs will be recommended a prescriptive template.
D2: Implement fast-path variant as an optional companion artifact; runtime will enforce a contract (schema + basic quality thresholds) before allowing traffic diversion.
D3: Canary spike runner will be implemented in the control plane with pluggable profiles (light, medium, heavy).
implementation_notes: ENG scope (ENG-4201): Add controller webhooks, pre-warm scheduling, and cooldown logic in the autoscaler service.
ENG scope (ENG-4278): Instrumentation changes to emit initialization_phase and kv_cache_warm_time; update trace sampling rules.
PM scope: Author prescriptive templates and console UI copy; coordinate with Solutions to prepare recommended defaults for enterprise customers.
QA scope: Develop CI chaos tests and build a reproducible spike harness that can run against test clusters.
SRE/Infra scope: Update capacity planning models to account for pre-warm influence and cost estimates.
